title: A Bogoliubov-ratio framework for quantum-information diagnostics of time-dependent two-mode Boson Hamiltonian
authors: Shi-Cheng Liu, Lei-Hua Liu, Bichu Li, Yuebing Zhou, Hai-Qing Zhang
abstract: We present a compact and unified framework for quantum-information diagnostics of time-dependent two-mode bosonic systems based on the Bogoliubov ratio $λ_k(η) \equiv β_k(η)/α_k(η)$. For a general time-dependent quadratic two-mode Hamiltonian, the state dynamics is exactly reduced to a single complex Riccati equation for $λ_k$. Upon tracing out one partner mode, the spectrum of the one-mode reduced density matrix is determined entirely by the squared magnitude $q_k(η) = \vert{}λ_k(η)\vert{}^2$. Consequently, we could construct the explicit, model-independent formula for the for the reduced-state purity, linear entropy, Rényi-2 entropy, and von Neumann entropy without reconstructing and diagonalizing the reduced density matrix on a model-by-model basis using coupled squeezing parameters ($r_k, φ_k$). We demonstrate the utility of this framework in two distinct non-stationary setups: primordial cosmological perturbations and a chirped-pulse nondegenerate optical parametric amplifier. In the cosmological context, our formulation clarifies how background-induced phase rotation and frequency softening regulate squeezing growth and state mixedness; in the optical domain, it captures the delayed onset, suppression of squeezing accumulation, and late-time entropy saturation induced by finite pump duration and frequency chirp. By cleanly factorizing model-dependent driving protocols from universal information-theoretic metrics, this framework offers an efficient, standardized diagnostic tool for a broad class of parametrically driven quadratic bosonic systems.
summary: The paper introduces the Bogoliubov-ratio framework to diagnose quantum information measures for any time-dependent two-mode bosonic system described by a quadratic Hamiltonian. By mapping the dynamics onto a single Riccati equation using the ratio $\lambda_k$, it allows researchers to calculate entanglement and purity metrics model-independently. This method is demonstrated in diverse physical settings, including cosmology and advanced optical parametric amplification.
main_problem: The goal is to create a unified, model-independent framework for diagnosing quantum information properties of time-dependent two-mode bosonic systems.
main_result: The state dynamics are entirely characterized by the Bogoliubov ratio $\lambda_k$, which allows for the direct calculation of various entanglement and purity measures without full density matrix reconstruction.
method: The framework utilizes the Bogoliubov ratio $\lambda_k =  eta_k/\alpha_k$ to reduce the complex state evolution governed by a quadratic Hamiltonian into a single, solvable Riccati differential equation.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by a general time-dependent two-mode bosonic Hamiltonian, applied successfully to both primordial cosmological perturbations and chirped-pulse nondegenerate optical parametric amplifiers.
key_observables: Reduced-state purity, linear entropy, Rényi-2 entropy, and von Neumann entropy, all derived from the squared magnitude $q_k = |\lambda_k|^2$.
important_parameters: The time-dependent coefficients $\omega_k(\eta)$ (frequency/detuning) and $g_k(\eta)$ (coupling/squeezing strength) govern the evolution of $\lambda_k$.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the system's dynamics can be mapped onto a normalized paired Bogoliubov representation, and it is valid for quadratic Hamiltonians.

paper_structure: The paper introduces the framework using a general Hamiltonian, derives the governing Riccati equation for $\lambda_k$, and then demonstrates its utility by applying it sequentially to two distinct physical examples: cosmology and optical parametric amplification.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, standardized diagnostic tool that cleanly separates the physics of the driving protocol (model-dependent) from universal quantum information metrics, which is highly valuable for analyzing complex open or time-varying bosonic systems in AMO/Optics.
